classification.difficultyReason: Construct two different connected, cycle-free subgraphs using all vertices, including a graph with parallel edges.

content.prompt: Draw two different spanning trees for each of these graphs.

spec.description: Six labelled vertices in the source arrangement; ordinary edges and markers use house black.
spec.mathematics: Vertices A, B, C, D, E, F; edges AB, AC, AD, BD, CD, CE, DE, DF, EF. Undirected and unweighted.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens are permanent; no spanning tree is selected.

answer.short: One possible tree: $AB, AC, CD, DE, DF$.
answer.worked: There are 6 vertices, so retain $6-1=5$ edges. Remove $AD, BD, CE, EF$. The remaining edges $AB, AC, CD, DE, DF$ connect all six vertices without a cycle.

spec.description: First example spanning tree, retaining the supplied vertex positions.
spec.mathematics: Edges AB, AC, CD, DE, DF connect six vertices with five edges and no cycle.

answer.short: Another possible tree: $AB, BD, CD, CE, EF$.
answer.worked: Remove $AC, AD, DE, DF$. Retain $AB, BD, CD, CE, EF$: these form the path $A-B-D-C-E-F$. All six vertices are connected by five edges, with no cycle.

spec.description: Second example spanning tree with a different edge set.
spec.mathematics: Edges AB, BD, CD, CE, EF form a path through all six vertices.

spec.description: Five labelled vertices, outer curved AC edge and two distinct AD edges. Ordinary source colours become house black.
spec.mathematics: Nine undirected edges: AB, BC, BD, CD, CE, DE, AC, direct AD and curved AD. No weights or arrows.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens are permanent; neither parallel edge is removed in the question.

answer.short: One possible tree: $AB, BC, CD, DE$.
answer.worked: There are 5 vertices, so retain $5-1=4$ edges. Remove both $AD$ edges, $AC, BD$ and $CE$. The remaining path $A-B-C-D-E$ connects all five vertices without a cycle.

spec.description: First example spanning tree using the original vertex positions.
spec.mathematics: Edges AB, BC, CD, DE form a five-vertex path.

answer.short: Another possible tree: $AC, BC, CE$ and the direct $AD$ edge.
answer.worked: Remove $AB, BD, CD, DE$ and the curved $AD$ edge. Retain $AC, BC, CE$ and the direct $AD$ edge. These four edges connect all five vertices without a cycle.

spec.description: Second example spanning tree retaining outer AC and direct AD.
spec.mathematics: Edges AC, BC, CE and direct AD connect five vertices with four edges and no cycle.
